newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slide as investors stay away.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slide as investors stay away.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.40 percent on Wednesday, slipping for eight trading sessions in a row, as an absence of foreign investors continued to discourage activity, traders said.
"Trading activity will remain at such poor levels as long as costs of setting up custody accounts remain unknown," one trader said.
The central bank ordered international investors to open custody accounts at Slovenian banks if they want to trade in Slovenian securities.
The eleven-share SBI index fell 5.42 points to 1,362.1. Since February 17, the blue-chip index dropped 7.2 percent.
Total turnover fell to 117.8 million tolars from 176.7 million and traders said trading activity would remain at a low ebb until fresh incentives surfaced.
Overall 10 shares fell, six rose and two were unchanged, while eight were untraded.
Bank SKB was the most active share, easing 0.36 percent to 55,000 tolars on volume of 838 shares for total turnover of 46.9 million.
Construction company GPG was the leading decliner, falling 7.16 percent to 7,000 tolars on volume of 120 shares.
Brokerage Primofin led the day's gainers, jumping 9.87 percent to 12,250 tolars on volume of 81 sharess. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
